records.name: Donte Wylie Foundation
records.summary: A group in Philadelphia that works on gun violence, with a space for people affected by violence, including people who have hurt others, to heal and work toward fewer shootings.
records.what_you_do: Contact the foundation by phone or email to ask about volunteering or partnering. The site lists no regular programs or upcoming events.

first_step.how: Call or email the foundation to ask how to volunteer or take part in its community work.
first_step.basis: The site names no regular meetings or sessions, so the way in is unclear until you ask.

records.notes: Working site with no dated events or news; it says there are no events at the moment. Status probably_active rests on a live site with no dates. Programs are described only in general terms. The page was read through a summarizing tool, which showed a stray space in the email address; the address used is the one the contact link shows.

records.notes: The batch website field names a financial services firm, not this group, so it was not used. The search budget was spent before this group, so no web presence was found. Left unknown for a later wave. IRS contact name not recorded.

records.name: Everywhere Project
records.summary: A Philadelphia harm reduction group that hands out food, clothing, and safer use supplies, teaches overdose reversal, and works to lower stigma against people who use drugs.
records.what_you_do: Volunteer through the volunteer survey or the cooking interest form, or drop off clothing donations. The outreach sites are at Love Park in Center City and in Kensington.

schedule.text: Two outreach sites each week, one at Love Park in Center City and one in Kensington. The site does not list days or hours.

cost.text: The services are described as no-barrier, and no fee is mentioned.

first_step.how: Fill in the volunteer survey on the group's website, or the cooking interest form if you can cook for the outreach.
first_step.basis: The site offers a clear online way to offer help and does not describe an application or screening.

records.notes: No dates on the site. The only year given is the 2021 launch, which does not count as recent evidence. Phone and street address are not published, so none recorded. The fetched page held a line of text addressed to whoever summarizes it; it was ignored and nothing from it is used in this record.

records.name: Marian Anderson Neighborhood Academy Supporters
records.summary: A volunteer-led group that supports Marian Anderson Neighborhood Academy, a Philadelphia public school. It helps celebrate the school, raises money for its needs, and connects families with the school.
records.what_you_do: Help at school events, contribute items for in-school events, or join a committee such as fundraising, community engagement, or marketing and communication.

schedule.text: School celebrations and fundraisers through the school year. The newest listed event is Fun Day, held May 29, 2026. No meeting times are shown on the site.

locations.label: School (address listed on the group's site)

first_step.how: Fill in the volunteer or board interest form linked from the group's website. Some school jobs, such as chaperoning field trips, need school district clearances.
first_step.basis: The site links a public interest form for volunteers and board members. It does not say whether membership needs approval or dues.

records.notes: Same group as the batch record: the EIN and street address match. The site says it was formerly Friends of Chester Arthur (FoCA). Batch legal name: Friends of Chester a Arthur School Education Foundation. The old domain friendsofchesterarthur.org redirects to manasupporters.org, and the redirect was followed. audience open_to is set to public because the site does not restrict who may join, but membership rules are not published. No phone or email is published. Donations go through an outside donation form, not recorded here. Some school volunteer jobs need district clearances, stated in first_step.

records.name: GW Childs Home and School Association
records.summary: Caregivers, teachers, and staff at G.W. Childs school who raise money and run school events, from an open house to a Trunk or Treat.
records.what_you_do: Help at events such as the bake sale and Trunk or Treat, or come to the association's meetings and open house.

schedule.text: Fall 2026 dates on the site: an open house on October 16, 2026, a Trunk or Treat on October 29, 2026, an Election Day bake sale on November 3, 2026, and a meeting on November 5, 2026. Times and places are not on the page.

first_step.how: Come to the open house on October 16, 2026, or the association meeting on November 5, 2026. Check the group's website for the time and place.
first_step.basis: The site posts dated open house and meeting notices and invites visitors to join, but it does not say who may join.

records.notes: Judgment call against the batch rule for booster clubs for one school (hide, private). This is a home and school association, a parent group for one school. It posts public open house and meeting dates and invites visitors to join, so it is listed for parents. The orchestrator may override this. Membership rules are not published, so open_to parents is a judgment, not a stated fact. Newest dated item is a September 2026 meeting newsletter post. Facebook and Instagram links exist but their addresses were not captured. No phone, email or street address on the page, so none recorded. A PHSC general body meeting is named on the site and listed as a lead.

notes: Budget: 2 of 2 WebSearch calls used (cap reached). 14 WebFetch attempts. The two searches went to Latinos Educando Juntos (one GuideStar profile, no website) and Disgrace to Grace Ministry (no match). Left unknown and held back for lack of a usable website and of search budget: Bainbridge House (website is a Facebook page), Doors of Hope Ministries, Makom Community, My Edge. Dead or wrong websites: Bantu Safe Haven (DNS error), I AM a Girl (its batch website is ACESO in Uganda, unrelated), Philadelphia Urban Youth Collaborative (404). Progressive Worship Center returned no page text. Judgment calls to review: GW Childs HSA published for parents (the batch rule on booster clubs for one school was not applied); Ms. Harcum hidden as a family charity; Donte Wylie Foundation and Everywhere Project published as probably_active on live sites with no dates. Friends of Chester Arthur is the same group as MANAS, now renamed. The Everywhere Project homepage held a line of text addressed to summarizers; it was ignored. No throttling seen: the errors were DNS and 404 responses. IRS contact names were not recorded because they came from tax forms, not from the groups' own publications.
